notes.summary: Simple Interest grows by the same amount every year; Compound Interest earns interest on interest. 1–2 questions are common in both tiers.

concepts.title: Simple Interest
concepts.body: SI = P × R × T / 100. Amount = P + SI. A sum becomes n times in T years when R × T = (n − 1) × 100.

concepts.title: Compound Interest
concepts.body: A = P(1 + R/100)<sup>T</sup>; CI = A − P. For 10% over 2 years, CI is 21% of P; over 3 years, 33.1%.

concepts.title: CI − SI difference
concepts.body: 2 years: D = P(R/100)<sup>2</sup>. 3 years: D = P(R/100)<sup>2</sup>(3 + R/100).

varieties.name: Simple Interest
varieties.how: Use SI = PRT/100 and solve for the unknown.

varieties.name: Compound Interest
varieties.how: Multiply by (1 + R/100) each year, or use the effective % (21% for 10% over 2 years).

varieties.name: Difference between CI and SI
varieties.how: Use D = P(R/100)<sup>2</sup> for 2 years and D = P(R/100)<sup>2</sup>(3 + R/100) for 3 years.

example.q: CI − SI on ₹ 10000 at 10% for 2 years?

tips: Amounts after consecutive years in CI form a GP: rate = (A<sub>2</sub> − A<sub>1</sub>)/A<sub>1</sub> × 100.
traps: Half-yearly compounding: halve the rate and double the time.
Questions may ask for amount, not interest; read carefully.

questions.q: Find the simple interest on ₹ 5,000 at 8% per annum for 3 years.
What is the compound interest on ₹ 10,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.solution:
Doubles → SI = P in 8 years.
P = P × R × 8/100 → R = 100/8 = 12.5%.

questions.q: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on a sum for 2 years at 5% per annum is ₹ 15. Find the sum.
A sum of money amounts to ₹ 6,050 in 2 years and to ₹ 6,655 in 3 years at compound interest. Find the sum.
What is the difference between compound interest and simple interest on ₹ 8,000 for 3 years at 10% per annum?
